unmapped_findings: Density of the solution-treated low-density steels depends linearly on alloying content: ho = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (g/cm³, with C, Al and Mn in mass%), Eq. (3); fitted coefficients for Al (0.10) and Mn (0.01) agree with published values while the C coefficient (0.102) is far smaller than the previously reported 0.41 g/cm³ per 1% C.

Both the ultimate true stress (~1350 MPa) and fracture true stress (~2150 MPa) were nearly constant for all investigated compositions, independent of alloying content and microstructure (ferrite fraction, austenite grain size, twin boundary fraction).

The strength of the solution-treated low-density steels is controlled mainly by κ-carbide size: yield strength and tensile strength scale linearly with the square root of κ-carbide diameter (slope ~97.1 MPa/nm^0.5, Fig. 7a), and ductility (elongation to failure, area reduction) as well as Charpy impact toughness decrease with increasing κ-carbide size, consistent with a particle-shear strengthening mechanism (Eq. 4).
Charpy impact toughness at −40 °C ranged from 354 J (Fe30Mn6Al1C) to 1.5 J (Fe30Mn11Al1.5C); values below 10 J occurred for C content above 1.2%, Mn content below 25%, and Al content above 10%.
The optimum combination (yield strength 642 MPa, ductility 72%, impact toughness 247 J, density 6.69 g/cm³) was obtained for Fe30Mn10Al1C after 1050 °C solution treatment.
